question: does staged curriculum training plus grounding data improve this model at this budget?
answer: Not yet, on general held-out data; the self-observation probe moved slightly.

curriculum.note: per-stage val losses are computed on each stage's OWN held-out slice and are therefore NOT comparable across stages

head_to_head_same_heldout.data: last 40 records of corpus.jsonl, identical for both checkpoints
head_to_head_same_heldout.verdict: the curriculum checkpoint is marginally WORSE on general held-out text (+0.018 CE). It spent its last 3.9 M tokens on stage-ordered domain data at a low learning rate, so this is not a refutation of curriculum training — it is a refutation of claiming a win at this budget.

self_observation.verdict: small movement (0.521 -> 0.568) at n=240; direction is right but the effect is too weak to call a capability. Behavioural grounding on negatives was 0/6 — the model never emitted 'not recorded', so citation discipline did NOT transfer.

why.tokens_vs_needed: 3.87 M tokens this run, 5.47 M cumulative. Compute-optimal at 19.3 M parameters is roughly 20x parameters in tokens = ~390 M. We are at ~1.4% of that.
why.compute: CPU-only, ~1,100 tok/s, 2015 iMac; ~80 min for 3.9 M tokens
why.implication: no curriculum, grounding corpus or probe can substitute for tokens at this scale; the infrastructure is ready and the number that must change is the token count

what_was_actually_delivered: staged curriculum trainer built from registry metadata (tradition/lang/tier), runs end to end
725 grounding pairs, 600 of them negatives (the anti-confabulation half)
self-observation probe: does the model represent its own groundedness, measured per layer
honest head-to-head showing the curriculum did not beat the base model yet
